reason: The PROBLEM is real and code-accurate; the PROPOSED FIX is wrong, so this is refuted with a corrected fix rather than confirmed. Verified in the source: place() is the only caller of getBoundingClientRect for the tip, it runs once from show(), and lately.html:908 registers a resize listener for deswarm only — nothing re-places or retires #tip on scroll or resize. Driven in chromium: keyboard-focus the 41-day marquee mark and scroll .scroll 260px and the tip stays on, stranded 225px from its mark and sitting over the 'What this can't tell you' movement; touch-pin a mark at 390 and scroll 300px and the pinned black label stays at (68,344) while its mark travels to y=116; resize 390 to 768 while pinned and the tip is still at top 344 while the mark leaves the viewport entirely at (412,-88). The seat's exact figures are loose (332px measured 225px here; the section named is the limits movement, not 'What's quietly slipping') but the mechanism reproduces exactly, including their (x,344) resize coordinate, and nothing in interaction-check.mjs asserts scroll behaviour for the tip, so this is not a restatement of the gate. Severity 'defect' is the right class, not overstated: the label's own text stays true, Escape and tap-away still dismiss it, so the product is not asserting a falsehood, it is visibly wrong and passable. What sinks the finding is the fix. (1) It calls place(showing) from the scroll handler, and place() rewrites tip.innerHTML from dataset.tip on every call, so every scroll event re-parses the tip's markup and forces two layout reads for a position that has not changed content — thrash in the one handler that must stay cheap. (2) drop() on scroll-out is a regression on the very path the finding is trying to protect: drop() clears the tip but the mark keeps DOM focus, and no focus event fires when the reader scrolls it back, so a focus-visible mark sits on screen with no name — and the source's own comment records that the mark's title lives nowhere else on the surface. drop() is right for a touch pin, wrong for a focus-raised tip. (3) The tracker instruction is wrong about the code: hide(true) is never called anywhere in lately.html, so 'clear it in hide(true)' clears nothing; the site that actually needs handling is the plain hide() on pointerleave/blur.
sharpenedFix: Split place() into fill(el) (sets tip.innerHTML) and position(el) (the two clamped left/top writes), so show() calls both and the move handler calls only position(). Track the raiser in one variable: let showing = null, set in show(), cleared in drop() and in the plain hide() when it actually removes .on. Then: const onMove = () => { if (!showing) return; const live = pinned === showing || document.activeElement === showing || tip.classList.contains('on'); if (!live) return; const b = showing.getBoundingClientRect(); if (b.bottom < 0 || b.top > innerHeight) { if (pinned) drop(); else tip.classList.remove('on'); return; } tip.classList.add('on'); position(showing); }; wrapped in a requestAnimationFrame coalescer (let queued = false) so a scroll burst does at most one placement per frame. Register window.addEventListener('scroll', queueMove, { capture: true, passive: true }) — capture is required because scroll does not bubble off the .scroll container, and passive keeps it off the scroll path — and window.addEventListener('resize', queueMove) AFTER the existing resize listener for deswarm at line 908, since deswarm rewrites --row and strip.style.minHeight and therefore moves the marks; placing onMove first would re-place against pre-deswarm geometry. The difference from the seat's version: a focus-raised tip is hidden, not dropped, when its mark leaves the viewport, and returns when the mark scrolls back, so a focused mark is never left nameless; only a touch pin is retired.
breaks: Re-measure after it lands: (a) interaction-check.mjs in full — the touch block calls scrollIntoViewIfNeeded before tapping, which now fires a capture-phase scroll during the pin sequence, so 'a real touch on a mark names it', 'the tooltip stays inside a 390 window', 'a second touch on the same mark dismisses it' and 'a touch away from the marks dismisses it' can all shift timing; (b) the keyboard block, since the tip can now be re-added by onMove after a blur and the 'Escape dismisses it' assertion must still hold — drop() must clear showing or Escape becomes recoverable by a stray scroll; (c) the resize path at 390/768/1280/1440 with a pin held, confirming deswarm runs first and the tip lands on the moved mark; (d) the 'no sideways scroll' assertion at every viewport, because position() can now write a left value during a resize mid-reflow when innerWidth and the tip's own width disagree — keep the existing 8px clamps unchanged; (e) audit.mjs hit targets and motion, unaffected in principle but the tip now toggles .on outside a pointer event, so the 0.14s opacity transition can fire on scroll — verify it does not read as a flicker when a mark crosses the viewport edge, and consider suppressing the transition on the scroll-driven re-add.
